summary: Elevated 5xx baseline for small-embedding micro-batches correlated with TLS/keepalive churn and runtime CPU throttling
description:
Issue summary:
A sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) was detected starting 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC for a high-volume enterprise customer uploading many small embedding requests (<32 tokens). The error-rate did not manifest as a single large spike but as a raised baseline (approx +2.1% absolute error-rate on /v1/embeddings over 6 hours).

Impact:
- Customer job pipelines (bulk embedding uploader) report intermittent failures that fail the whole job due to immediate abort on non-200.
- Incidents observed across multiple edge hosts but concentrated on a subset of apigw instances handling the customer's traffic.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood API (prod us-east-1)
- API route: POST /v1/embeddings
- Customer account: Pattern Health (enterprise)
- Affected model: open-embed-small-v1 pinned on their integration

Timeline & quick signals:
- 2026-03-12 21:50 UTC: first minor uptick detected by SLO alerting (embeddings 5xx rate > 0.5%).
- 2026-03-12 22:05 UTC: elevated baseline confirmed across three edge clusters.
- 2026-03-12 23:40 UTC: initial mitigation (edge keepalive timeout bump) rolled to 10 hosts.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create batch of 100 embedding requests with batch_size=1-4 and concurrency=80 from a single IP range.
2) Send to customer API key pinned to open-embed-small-v1.
3) Observe ~2-3% 502/503s intermittently within 10 minutes.

Logs / diagnostic snippets:
- apigw log excerpt: "upstream_response_time=0.012 upstream_status=502 upstream_addr=10.10.84.92:443 recv_error='tls: unexpected message'"
- edge-proxy: "keepalive reused with different ALPN - closing" repeated ~3k times over 1h on host apigw-84
- runtime syslog: "watchdog: cpu quota exceeded, force-exit pid=1423 signal=SIGABRT" on several runtime pods (same tenant)
- tcpdump (sample): repeated TLS client hello renegotiation followed by RST from edge proxy

Initial hypothesis:
1) Recent edge TLS keepalive/ALPN change caused intermittent session reuse failures for a subset of clients leading to upstream proxy errors (tls: unexpected message).
2) Small, high-concurrency micro-bursts of tiny embedding requests cause CPU scheduling pressure in the serving-runtime cgroup, triggering watchdog resets when combined with proxy retries.
3) The combination amplifies retries on the apigw side, raising the observed 5xx baseline rather than a single large spike.

Immediate actions taken:
- Increased keepalive timeout and disabled HTTP/1.1 pipelining on suspected apigw hosts (apigw-80..apigw-89) as a precautionary mitigation.
- Temporarily bumped CPU quota for the serving-runtime pool handling the tenant to reduce watchdog-triggered exits.
- Enabled extra logging (TLS handshakes and socket reuse traces) for 2h window.
- Instructed customer to throttle concurrency to 30 for immediate workaround.

Current status / next steps:
- Status: In Progress, assigned to Marco Reyes (SRE) to continue deep-dive.
- Capture core dumps from two affected runtime pods (collection in progress).
- Run controlled reproducer in staging with identical pinning and request pattern.
- If keepalive/ALPN codepath rollback is possible, prepare canary rollback on 5 hosts.
- Plan canary of revised runtime cgroup config for this tenant during low-traffic window (0300-0400 UTC).

Workaround for customer:
- Reduce concurrency to <=30 for embedding small-batch uploads OR use larger batch_size (>=16) to amortize CPU per-request overhead.
- Optionally migrate to Dedicated capacity until root cause is resolved (support can assist with expedited dedicated trial).

investigation: Collected artifacts: apigw logs, edge-proxy traces, tcpdump from apigw-84, core dumps from two runtime pods, and SLO time series. Initial correlation analysis shows error-rate concentrated on apigw hosts that recently received TLS/ALPN configuration change. Core dumps show runtime experiencing scheduling starvation in the small-embed preprocessing path under high concurrency, triggering a watchdog exit. Reproducer in staging with identical concurrency pattern reproduces increased error-rate; disabling HTTP/1.1 pipelining on the edge eliminated the tls: unexpected message symptom but runtime exits persisted until CPU quota bump. Next: validate whether rolling back TLS change prevents session reuse mismatch and whether adding micro-backoff in preprocessor eliminates runtime watchdog exits.
resolution: Mitigations applied: keepalive/pipelining changes on edge hosts and a temporary CPU quota increase for runtime pool. Customer workaround (reduced concurrency or larger batches) accepted. Engineering PR proposed to add micro-backoff when processing tiny embedding batches (PR #4210). Awaiting PR review, canary, and post-canary monitoring. Final resolution will be documented after canary completes and postmortem is written.
